question: In her September 2026 State of the Union address, President von der Leyen announced a new EU water initiative, noting growing water scarcity and water’s importance for agriculture, energy, industry and food security. The announcement comes a year after the European water resilience strategy was adopted.

The strategy sets out over 50 actions to improve water management and places implementation of the Water Framework Directive among its top priorities. What is more, the Commission had already announced its intention to revise the Water Framework Directive, despite the findings of its previous fitness check. 1.
What will be the goal, scope and added value of this initiative in comparison with the 2025 water resilience strategy and existing EU water legislation?
How will the initiative relate to the announced revision of the Water Framework Directive?

If the Commission sees a need for a new EU initiative to tackle water scarcity, how has it determined that the problem lies in the current water legislation framework rather than implementation, investment and enforcement gaps?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.11.2026) The summer drought of 2026 demonstrated the growing risk of water scarcity and the scale of related damages across the EU. While economic impacts of drought are still ongoing and are in general difficult to assess, one bank estimated the damage to amount to EUR 180 billion1.

Droughts account for 54% of agricultural losses in the EU and climate-related agricultural losses are estimated at around EUR 28.3 billion per year2. Currently events of floodings are causing concerns and putting citizens and business at risk. In response to these circumstances, the President of the Commission announced in her State of the Union the European Water Initiative.

The initiative will further enhance action on water resilience in general, addressing especially risks of water scarcity across economic sectors. It will build on the 2025 Water Resilience Strategy3 and seek synergies with other relevant policy instruments. Work on the European Water Initiative is ongoing.
Its exact form and content will be determined taking into consideration all relevant parameters and building among others on broad consultation with stakeholders.
